- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. # Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A missing ELF must fail in the driver with a clear "ELF not found", BEFORE any
# engine is launched -- never the cryptic downstream
# "qemu-system-riscv64: Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS ...".
# Covers fast (the reported case) + cycle; hybrid already guarded (regression).
# The fix lives at the one shared resolver (abs_elf), so fast/cycle/cycle-gdb
# all inherit it; this test pins fast + cycle + hybrid.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "need build/andesim"

MISSING="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/__definitely_absent__.elf"
[ -e "$MISSING" ] && fail "test bug: $MISSING unexpectedly exists"

# assert_missing <label> <args...>: run the driver, require a non-zero exit, the
# driver's own "ELF not found" diagnostic, and the ABSENCE of any engine spawn
# ("Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS" proves qemu was reached -- it must not be).
assert_missing() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "$label: missing ELF should exit non-zero, got 0: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'ELF not found' \
    || fail "$label: missing the 'ELF not found' diagnostic: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS' \
    && fail "$label: reached qemu instead of failing in the driver: $out"
  ok "$label: missing ELF -> clean 'ELF not found', no engine spawn"
}

# fast: the reported bug -- must not hand the missing path to qemu.
assert_missing "fast" run --mode fast "$MISSING"

# cycle: reaches the shared resolver only after engine discovery + selection, so
# it needs a concrete --engine (and VSIM_BIN_DIR for discovery). The existence
# check is arch-independent -- elf_xlen of a missing file is 0, so no arch
# mismatch fires first regardless of which engine we pick.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
export VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR"
eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$eng" ]; then
  assert_missing "cycle" run --mode cycle --engine "$eng" "$MISSING"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle: no vsim engine discoverable under $BINDIR"
fi

# hybrid: already validates existence up front -- regression guard.
assert_missing "hybrid" run --mode hybrid "$MISSING"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run trigger/pc gating: --trigger / --pc-start / --pc-end are the hybrid ROI
# delimiters. fast/cycle used to silently IGNORE them -- a user asking for a
# pc window got a whole-program cycle figure with no warning. They are now
# rejected (rc 2) on any model except hybrid.
#
#   1. cycle/fast + --trigger          -> usage error (rc 2)
#   2. cycle/fast + --pc-end           -> usage error (rc 2)
#   3. cycle/fast + --pc-start         -> usage error (rc 2)
#   5. hybrid + --trigger pc + pc-*    -> never gated (reaches the ELF check)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
MISSING=/no/such/file.elf

# 1-3. fast/cycle reject the hybrid-only ROI knobs (real ELF: pre-gate these
# ran the whole program and returned 0; the gate must now turn them into rc 2).
expect 2 'trigger applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --trigger pc \
  --pc-start 0x100074 --pc-end 0x100080 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'trigger applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --trigger marker "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-end applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --pc-end 0x100080 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-start applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --pc-start 0x100074 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-start applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --pc-start 0x100074 "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "fast/cycle reject --trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end"

# 5. hybrid is the home of these flags: never gated, reaches the ELF check.
expect 2 'ELF not found' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
  --pc-start 0x100074 --pc-end 0x100080 "$MISSING"
ok "hybrid --trigger pc not gated"

ok "run trigger/pc gating (hybrid-only)"

        --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"

## Findings

**1. `driver/cmd_run.cpp` — `run_hybrid()` (lines 345-348): duplicates `abs_elf()`'s existence check.**
After the diff, `abs_elf()` does exactly what `run_hybrid` hand-rolls inline:
```cpp
const fs::path elf = fs::absolute(cli.positional[0], ec);
if (ec || !fs::is_regular_file(elf, ec))
  return fail("ELF not found: " + cli.positional[0]);
```
`abs_elf`'s own comment even says "Mirrors the up-front check run_hybrid already does." It **can** call `abs_elf` instead, and the message is byte-identical:
- `run_hybrid` prints `andesim run --mode hybrid: ELF not found: <path>` (via `fail`).
- `abs_elf(cli.positional[0], "--mode hybrid")` prints `andesim run --mode hybrid: ELF not found: <path>` (the `is_regular_file` branch) — same string, same exit (returns `""` → `return 2`).

One adaptation cost: `run_hybrid` keeps the `fs::path elf` for `elf.stem()` at lines 437 and 514, whereas `abs_elf` returns `std::string`. So the replacement is `const std::string elf_path = abs_elf(...); if (elf_path.empty()) return 2;` plus `fs::path(elf_path).stem()` at those two cosmetic lines. The only behavioral divergence is the ultra-rare `fs::absolute` failure branch (`abs_elf` says "cannot resolve ELF", hybrid said "ELF not found") — not hit by any test and arguably more accurate.
**Cost: ~4 lines of the resolve+exists+error sequence duplicated, now that `abs_elf` is the shared resolver.**

**2. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_missing_elf.sh` — `assert_missing()`: NOT a re-implementation. Clean.**
It overlaps `expect()` (rc check + positive grep) but adds a **negative** assertion `expect` cannot express — that the output must NOT contain `Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS` (the whole point: prove no engine was spawned) — plus a `timeout 30` wrapper and per-label messaging. The sibling `test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` already establishes the same hand-roll pattern for richer-than-`expect` assertions (lines 30-35, 72-77). The test correctly **reuses** `fail`/`ok`/`vsim_bin_dir` from `tests/lib/log.sh` (lines 12, 43) rather than re-implementing them. No reuse issue.

## Summary
- Finding 1 (`run_hybrid` ↔ `abs_elf`): real, actionable — collapse the inline existence check into `abs_elf("--mode hybrid")`; messages match exactly.
- Finding 2 (test): clean — the negative BIOS-absence check is load-bearing and beyond `expect`'s reach; helpers from `log.sh` are reused, not duplicated.
